sense.text:
“They search out iniquities; they accomplish a diligent search.” That is what the archaeologists are paid to do. Hundreds of thousands of dollars, if not millions, go into these digs, and they do a diligent search to uncover the truth in history. And they uncover the black Egyptians of the past, the black slaves on the tomb walls.

Then Hollywood gets access to all of it and says, let’s make Moses white, let’s make the Pharaohs white, everybody from France. That is how you know it is all evil.

“Both the inward thought of every one of them, and the heart, is deep.” They do a deep, diligent search, and what they find, they use. America took the holidays and customs these digs uncovered: they did not want the truth of who the people were, but they took Christmas, they took Easter, Ishtar. It all goes back to this.

“Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph.” This is the New Kingdom, the 18th dynasty. Before it, the Hyksos, the shepherds out of Palestine, had ruled the Delta in the 15th dynasty, until the 17th dynasty Thebans drove them out and ushered in the New Kingdom. This new family on the throne did not recognize Joseph. They never heard of him, and they did not give a damn about what Joseph did for the dynasty before them.

He says the children of Israel “are more and mightier than we”, and fears that “when there falleth out any war, they join also unto our enemies, and fight against us.” Put yourself there: a race that had been living free from the time of Joseph, and now a new Pharaoh says, let’s enslave them. Do you think it was an easy thing, that we just stood there and let them put shackles on our necks? No. There was fight. There was war.

That is why the chained captives on the plaques Ramses the Second set up in honor of his warriors can be Israelites even though they are called war captives. Look at the yokes on their necks with the hooks at the ends: they are just like the yokes on the Negro in America. America did the same things ancient Egypt did.

“Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens.” They made the children of Israel slaves, and they built for Pharaoh the treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses. The paintings out of the tombs show it: Israelites working in the fields and vineyards for Pharaoh, picking olives and grapes under the taskmasters, and every one of them black. You cannot get a white man out of those.

“Joseph, being seventeen years old, was feeding the flock with his brethren.” Hold on to that age. Joseph is a teenager, seventeen, when all of this begins, and it is going to matter when we see how old he is when he finally stands before Pharaoh.
Judah says, “What profit is it if we slay our brother, and conceal his blood? Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmeelites, and let not our hand be upon him; for he is our brother and our flesh.”

“Then there passed by Midianites merchantmen”, and they “sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver.” People always have questions about the Midianites and the Ishmeelites. They were together. They were roaming the land together, working together, all Abraham’s children.
“And Reuben returned unto the pit; and, behold, Joseph was not in the pit; and he rent his clothes.” Reuben went back to save Joseph. That is why he said put him in the pit: his plan was to save him.

They could not explain Joseph not being there, so they concocted a story. They “killed a kid of the goats, and dipped the coat in the blood”, and brought the coat of many colours to their father, and Jacob said, “an evil beast hath devoured him.” The brothers were so envious of Joseph, very envious, and envy will have you do some evil stuff.

“And the Midianites sold him into Egypt unto Potiphar.” Although it says Midianites here and Ishmeelites before, it is not a contradiction. They worked closely together, they were always together, and they looked very similar.

precepts.why:
Abraham took another wife, Keturah, “And she bare him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah.” Six sons from Abraham, and Midian is one of them. Then the sons of Jokshan, of Dedan, and of Midian: “All these were the children of Keturah.”

So the Midianites who drew Joseph out of the pit are Abraham’s children through Keturah.

“Now these are the generations of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah’s handmaid, bare unto Abraham.” Ishmael had sons too, “twelve princes according to their nations”, living “by their towns, and by their castles.”

Abraham’s children from Keturah and Abraham’s children from Hagar always lived together and worked together. That is why Genesis 37 can say the Midianites drew Joseph out of the pit and sold him to the Ishmeelites, and then say the Midianites sold him into Egypt, and Genesis 39 say Potiphar bought him of the hands of the Ishmeelites. They were one company, all Abraham’s kids.

sense.text: Potiphar “bought him of the hands of the Ishmeelites, which had brought him down thither.” Genesis 37:36 said the Midianites sold him unto Potiphar; here it is the Ishmeelites. They were together, and they looked very similar.

“The Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man.” Joseph is in slavery now, but he was faithful to Potiphar, and Potiphar raised him up: “he made him overseer over his house, and all that he had he put into his hand.”
“The Lord blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake.” The theme is the same as when Jacob worked for Laban all those years, and Laban was blessed for Jacob’s sake.

His master’s wife “cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie with me.” Have sex with me. “But he refused.” Joseph told her his master had kept back nothing from him “but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?” Notice Joseph was not blaming God that he was in slavery. He was still fearing God in it.

“As she spake to Joseph day by day.” This was not one time. She was trying to wear him down day by day. And the Egyptians did not marry ugly women; remember when Abraham went down there, he knew they would take Sarah because she was beautiful. So Potiphar’s wife was a skank, but she was not a bad looking one. She was good on the eyes, and Joseph still said no: you are my master’s wife, I cannot touch you.

“He left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out.” He got the hell out of dodge. He saw sin like a snake and ran like a rabbit, and he was seventeen. Everybody says, I would run. Half of y’all have been put out for adultery two and three times. Let’s take a page out of what our forefather Joseph did.

When she could not get her way, she lied: “See, he hath brought in an Hebrew unto us to mock us.” Here is the lying woman who cannot get her way, so she will lie and get you locked up. Some brothers have been locked up because of a wife, an ex-wife or an ex-girlfriend the same way: she wants your life to go down the tubes, calls you over, and when you refuse her she will bust herself upside the head and tell the cops you did it.

“She laid up his garment by her, until his lord came home.” She kept his clothes until her husband came home.

It is the same spirit that put many of our people to death in slavery. Emmett Till was put to death on the word of a lying white woman, and there are a lot of cases like that.
“His wrath was kindled.” A lot of brothers are in jail because their woman will start a fight and expect him to defend her. Don’t deal with a woman like that. That is the kind of woman Potiphar had.

Joseph’s master “put him into the prison, a place where the king’s prisoners were bound.” Remember he is seventeen. Joseph’s family was rich; Jacob was wealthy. He was taken from all of that, and now he is in the midst of poverty, in jail, in prison.

“The Lord was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison.” The keeper committed all the prisoners to Joseph’s hand, “and that which he did, the Lord made it to prosper.” Whatever Joseph did, the Lord made it to prosper, even in prison.

precepts.why:
“He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.” That explains why Joseph was raised up. He was in slavery, but he was faithful to Potiphar, and Potiphar put all that he had into his hand.

It speaks to us. The Most High is observing us in whatever we are doing, and the least we are faithful in is these little jobs we get out here. Just like Joseph was in captivity, we are in captivity, and some think because we are in captivity we can steal, lie and rob. No, that is wrong. God is watching each and every one of us. On your jobs, don’t steal. Deal right.

“Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent.” That is what Joseph did when he left his garment in her hand and fled. If a snake fell into this room, everybody would be out of here. That snake is your sin.

It is not pork. It is not food, unless you are a fatty wad; if you are a fatty wad, that snake is food for you. For the rest of y’all, food is not your demon. It is generally sexual demons. Not everybody has the same demon. “For if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee: the teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men.” Them sexual demons will get you, brothers. Take a page out of what our forefather Joseph did at the age of seventeen.

“A backbiting tongue hath disquieted many, and driven them from nation to nation: strong cities hath it pulled down, and overthrown the houses of great men.” See what a backbiting tongue can do. Somebody that lies on you can do much destruction.

Read on to verse 18: “Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: but not so many as have fallen by the tongue.” The tongue does a lot of evil, and that is what Potiphar’s wife did to Joseph.

“My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” Joseph understood this, because his daddy taught him this.

“Set thy heart aright, and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble.” Make not haste means don’t leave this truth in your time of trouble. Satan will say, if you weren’t in that Bible you wouldn’t be going through half of what you are going through; you had it better when you served Satan. “Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end.”

“Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully, and be patient when thou art changed to a low estate.” That is the part we want. Joseph was changed from the house of a wealthy father to slavery and prison. Just as it goes for us, it went for our father Joseph.

“When a man’s ways please the Lord, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.” That is what happened with Joseph: the Lord was with him and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison, the very ones holding him bound.

sense.text: The butler and the baker said, “We have dreamed a dream, and there is no interpreter of it.” Joseph said, “Do not interpretations belong to God? tell me them, I pray you.”

“Make mention of me unto Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house.” He wanted out of that dungeon. Notice this calls the prison a dungeon: “here also have I done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.”
The baker’s interpretation: “Pharaoh lift up thy head from off thee, and shall hang thee on a tree.”

“It came to pass the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday.” Wherever you read of Pharaoh’s birthday, Herod’s birthday, the birthday of one of the Greek kings, something bad always happens. Here the baker was hanged. That is why we never celebrated birthdays: it is a day of narcissism, a day of proclaiming yourself to be God, of putting ourselves above God. You got it from the white man, who got it from his archaeological digs. It is not of God. It is of the devil.
“Yet did not the chief butler remember Joseph, but forgat him.”

precepts.why:
“The hopes of a man void of understanding are vain and false: and dreams lift up fools. Whoso regardeth dreams is like him that catcheth at a shadow, and followeth after the wind.” Don’t chase dreams.

But verse 3 gives a clue to understanding dreams from God: “The vision of dreams is the resemblance of one thing to another, even as the likeness of a face to a face.” You could dream about somebody you know named Joe, and you see Joe’s face, but it is not Joe. It is someone similar to Joe, maybe in age or in what they do for a living. It might be Bob. You have to know the people in your circle.

“They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and cast a stone upon me.” Another place where the prison is called the dungeon. The stone cast upon him means he would never get out. It is speaking of Israel in captivity, and it goes with the political prisoners who have been in there a long time.
Job said, “Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said, There is a man child conceived.” This is how the Hebrews felt regarding birthdays. We never celebrated them.

“Cursed be the day wherein I was born: let not the day wherein my mother bare me be blessed.” Jeremiah says the same thing Job said. We never celebrated birthdays: days of narcissism, days to put ourselves up above God. If you are still doing it and say it is for the children, shut up, you narcissist. Stop celebrating this evil.

sense.text: “At the end of two full years.” That does not tell you how long Joseph was in prison. He could have been far more than nineteen, and as we read on it shows that he was.
Ill favoured kine means those cows looked sickly. Seven fat ones and seven skinny ones, and the skinny ones ate up the fat.
“They brought him hastily out of the dungeon: and he shaved himself, and changed his raiment, and came in unto Pharaoh.”
“It is not in me: God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace.”
“For it shall be very grievous”, meaning very bad. The dream was doubled “because the thing is established by God”: that famine shall surely happen.

Joseph did not sleep. He told them exactly what to do: look out a man discreet and wise, appoint officers, take up the fifth part in the plenteous years, “and lay up corn under the hand of Pharaoh”, “that the land perish not through the famine.” To every problem we must have a solution. There are spirits among us that, for every solution, have a problem. Stay away from brothers or sisters like that.

“Only in the throne will I be greater than thou.” Joseph got elevated: the ring, the vestures of fine linen, the gold chain, the second chariot, “and they cried before him, Bow the knee.” We are going to tell the nations that too. Everybody is going to bow.
Pharaoh gave him to wife Asenath the daughter of Poti–pherah priest of On. Why did he not marry an Israelite? Because there were no other Israelites there.
“Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt.” He went in at seventeen and came out at thirty: thirteen years in prison. He was in prison much longer than we thought.
Manasseh means made to forget: God, said he, “hath made me forget all my toil.” Ephraim means fruitful: “God hath caused me to be fruitful in the land of my affliction.”

“In all the land of Egypt there was bread.” That is what it is like when you have a plan, a solution. Joseph did not sit around and wait for the dearth. The Most High showed him in a dream it was coming, and he said, I got a plan, this is what we are going to do about it. Whatever problems come or we foresee, we must start to move toward those solutions and make moves of preparation. That is how we have to be.

precepts.why:
“Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings.” Business means God’s business. Joseph was brought out of the dungeon to stand before Pharaoh.

That is why the brothers are now meeting dignitaries across the world: we have been diligent in God’s business. “He shall not stand before mean men.” Mean men are bums, obscure people, clowns on the internet with three followers who want to debate to get clout off of you. We don’t stand before bums. Stop talking to them; they are not worth your time.

“Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord.” That is the proof that the business in Proverbs 22:29 is God’s business: don’t be slothful when it comes to God’s business. Serving the Lord.
“Joseph, being seventeen years old.” He was seventeen when he went in, and Genesis 41:46 says he was thirty when he stood before Pharaoh. Thirteen years in prison. He came out at the age of thirty.

sense.text: Jacob did not send Benjamin, “Lest peradventure mischief befall him”: in case something bad happened.

Joseph’s brethren “bowed down themselves before him with their faces to the earth.” When they were younger, Joseph dreamed that his brothers bowed down to him, and they got mad at it. Now it is coming to pass.

“Joseph knew his brethren, but they knew not him.” They thought he was an Egyptian. They saw a black man in Egyptian garments speaking strange to them. That lets you know Joseph looked just like the Egyptians; he could not have been a Caucasian at all, or he would have stood out like a sore thumb.
“One is not” means one is dead.

“He spake unto them by an interpreter.” That added to it: Joseph spoke to them only through an Egyptian interpreter who understood Hebrew, as if he did not speak Hebrew. He did, and it made it more convincing that he was an Egyptian.
“He turned himself about from them, and wept.” Although they did evil to him, he still loved his brothers. He had to turn from them and cry privately.
“Ye shall traffick in the land”, meaning do business.
“Joseph is not, and Simeon is not”: Joseph is dead to him, Simeon is in prison, and now they want to take Benjamin away.

“Slay my two sons, if I bring him not to thee.” Remember what Reuben has been trying to do since they first put Joseph in the pit. He suggested the pit so he could go back and save him, and now he says kill my two sons if I don’t bring Benjamin back. That is the character of Reuben.

“And the famine was sore in the land.” There have always been famines. The only difference now is we think a famine could never happen, because we have been accustomed to plenty here. We are telling you famine is coming. Some of you are preparing; some of you are not.
Judah says the man solemnly protested, “Ye shall not see my face, except your brother be with you.” Bring your baby brother, Benjamin.
Judah says, “I will be surety for him; of my hand shalt thou require him.”

precepts.why:
Agabus “signified by the spirit that there should be great dearth throughout all the world: which came to pass in the days of Claudius Cesar.” It did not take place when Agabus saw it. He saw it under Caligula; Caligula was put to death; then Claudius came in, anywhere from five to ten years later, and it came to pass.

It is said for a reason. Famine is spoken of ahead of time, and it comes. We are telling you famine is coming.

“Behold, famine and plague, tribulation and anguish, are sent as scourges for amendment. But for all these things they shall not turn from their wickedness, nor be always mindful of the scourges.”

Scourges come among us: what happened with George Floyd was a scourge, 9/11 was a big scourge. But our people tend to forget. We got a little civil rights around 1964 and 1965, sixty-two years ago, and black people have forgotten and say it could never happen again. Now they are bringing back the vagrancy laws: if you are homeless you get arrested, and under the 13th Amendment the one arrested becomes a slave, picking the same crops they laughed at Issachar for picking. When Trump said make America great again, he said bring slavery back: making vagrancy laws great again, under the 13th Amendment. They are moving black congresswomen’s districts so they lose their seats. South Africans make like apartheid never existed, and here it is the same.

“Behold, victuals shall be so good cheap upon earth, that they shall think themselves to be in good case, and even then shall evils grow upon earth, sword, famine, and great confusion.” Things are so cheap you can walk down to the corner store and get all your food, and behind the scenes there is a lot of evil going on: talk of raising prices to keep black folks off the cruise ships, moving the supermarkets out of black communities so you have to drive twenty miles. And our people riot and burn down the stores instead of saving their money and opening their own, our own supermarket, our own Walmart.

It is the same stupidity as Idi Amin’s Uganda: he put the whites and Asians out of the country and gave Ugandans their businesses, but nobody had the expertise in the imports and exports, and the stores collapsed. It is the same in South Africa today, turning on the Ghanaians, Nigerians and others from that region who have legitimate little stores, blaming them for the jobs, putting them out of the hospitals, while white people own ninety percent of the business and ninety percent of the land. The enemies are in their face, and they turn against their own brothers. There is no difference between South Africa, Uganda and black people here: problems, and nobody with solutions. The white man’s solution is jail time, and you will be his slave once again when he takes you to prison.

“For many of them that dwell upon earth shall perish of famine; and the other, that escape the hunger, shall the sword destroy.” The Bible is telling you famine is going to be upon the earth, and you say never in America.

sense.text:
“Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read: no one of these shall fail, none shall want her mate.” No prophecy shall fail. You cannot mate another book with the Bible. Esau is now putting other books in with it: download a Bible app and it comes with all kinds of additional books, not the Apocrypha we have, but books like Enoch and Jasher.

The book of Jasher, in its account of Judah standing before Joseph for Benjamin, has Judah throw a stone four hundred shekels heavy to the heavens and sit on it till it turns to dust, Joseph command his son Manasseh to do the same with another stone, when Manasseh and Ephraim were little kids, Naphtali running on the ears of corn without breaking them, and Judah and his brethren scattering the whole army of Egypt with a shout. That did not happen. It makes nice fairy tale stuff, but it contradicts the biblical text. That is why we stay away from these books.

All the souls that came with Jacob into Egypt out of his loins were “threescore and six”, and with the two sons of Joseph born in Egypt, “all the souls of the house of Jacob, which came into Egypt, were threescore and ten.” Seventy.
Joseph “fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while. And Israel said unto Joseph, Now let me die, since I have seen thy face.”

Pay attention: Joseph tells his brethren to say, “Thy servants’ trade hath been about cattle from our youth”, “that ye may dwell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd is an abomination unto the Egyptians.” Every shepherd is an abomination unto the Egyptians, and that is why we go back to Genesis 43.
“His bowels did yearn upon his brother: and he sought where to weep; and he entered into his chamber, and wept there.”

“They set on for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians, which did eat with him, by themselves: because the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews; for that is an abomination unto the Egyptians.”

The Egyptians did not sit with the Hebrews to eat. Remember the Jim Crow times: it was an abomination for Esau to allow us to sit in their restaurants. The signs said, We serve whites only, no Spanish or Mexicans; no dogs and no Mexicans; El Paso, Texas, 1929. These were all across the South. We were forbidden their restaurants, their toilets, even their water fountains, and Issachar was included in that too; the Mexicans were classified as Negroes no matter how light their skin. The white man would not even sit down with us or pray with us. Some signs shut out the Jews too, and that is the only reason Amalek joined with us.

What we read about ancient Egypt, we think was for back then. No. This is recent, a little over sixty years ago. We got sixty-two years of a little civil rights and thought we had won the world, and in that time we have done the same thing South Africans have done since apartheid ended: nothing. We still don’t have our own hospitals, our own bus lines. Back then we had our own, and we gave it up to be integrated, Hellenized, assimilated. Now Esau is taking back all of it.

precepts.why:
“And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt.” This is the evidence that America is Egypt. The great city is Babylon the Great. Spiritually, not physically: this is not the real Sodom or the real Egypt, but it is a spiritual Sodom and a spiritual Egypt. America knows it: the pyramid on the dollar bill with 1776 at the bottom, Novus Ordo Seclorum, the obelisk in Washington, D.C. It is a spiritual Egypt where they have captured some of the tribes of Israel.

So the Egyptians who would not eat bread with the Hebrews are the same as the Esau who would not let us sit in his restaurants under Jim Crow.

“Where also our Lord was crucified.” Our Lord was crucified in Jerusalem. So this is not the real Jerusalem, but a spiritual Jerusalem: the same spirits that hated and murdered Christ are back again here in America, Babylon the Great. They hate Christ’s image and they hate his teachings.

sense.text: “Thy servants are shepherds, both we, and also our fathers.” Why did Joseph tell them to say they were shepherds? Because of the Hyksos. The Hyksos were shepherd kings out of Palestine who took over the Delta and founded the 15th dynasty, until the 17th dynasty Thebans drove them out. The Hyksos era came just before Joseph’s time, and Joseph knew that history: it was an abomination for the Egyptians to sit with shepherds. So he had them say they were shepherds, and they were set apart in Goshen.
“And when money failed in the land of Egypt.” This is very important. What good is money during a time of famine? Money is useless.

“There is not ought left in the sight of my lord, but our bodies, and our lands”; “buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be servants unto Pharaoh.” All they had left was their bodies and their land, and they sold both to be servants unto Pharaoh.

“And Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh”; “so the land became Pharaoh’s.” Pharaoh, under Joseph, bought all the land, the homes, everything.

That is happening now. Agenda 21 is a master plan out of the United Nations for total collectivism: people must not have private property or land of their own, they must live in high-rise apartments the state provides, dependent on the state for everything, because a man with a couple of acres, his own water and his own food cannot be controlled. Look at Blackstone and BlackRock buying up homes and building apartments all through America and controlling the rents. We never lost our lands; we lost our minds. And many with the knowledge will not speak it, because the paycheck dictates what comes out of their mouths.

You think it could never happen again, that a people would say, we need the government to take care of us, take our property, take everything, just give us food. Keep playing, as they move the grocery stores out of black communities and get rid of Section 8.

precepts.why:
“Behold, victuals shall be so good cheap upon earth, that they shall think themselves to be in good case, and even then shall evils grow upon earth, sword, famine, and great confusion.”

Even then shall evils grow. While you are eating, with victuals so cheap, things are going on behind the scenes: district lines moved, homeless laws made for imprisonment, the cheap airlines that black folks use taken away or their prices raised to keep black folks off. Slowly but surely it is moving toward what happened in Egypt.

“And in the latter time of their kingdom, when the transgressors are come to the full, a king of fierce countenance, and understanding dark sentences, shall stand up.” We are in the latter end; this is the era we are in now.

What was written aforetime was written for our learning. We read about Joseph and say, that’s a nice story, it can never happen again. Don’t fool yourself. There are people in this administration who look into and study the scriptures, more than four chapters a day.

“They search out iniquities; they accomplish a diligent search.” They have people whose job is to sit and study the scriptures from sunup to sundown and take notes. That is how we are getting to something so similar to the days of Joseph, when the famine came and everybody gave up their land to Pharaoh for bread. And while they search, our people keep playing games with adultery and lies; about eighty were put out for adultery this week.

“I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.” The history of Joseph in Egypt is a similitude. What happened then shows what is happening now. God does not have time for you to keep playing; time is not going to slow down.

sense.text: “The burden of Egypt.” This Egypt is Babylon the Great, the same as we read in Revelation 11:8, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt.

“And I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: and they shall fight every one against his brother.” That means civil war. Trump is paying the January 6th rioters for being arrested, when people died. Don’t be surprised if it is blue states against red states, Democrats against Republicans, “city against city, and kingdom against kingdom”, and everybody picks a side.
“And the spirit of Egypt shall fail in the midst thereof.” That great American battle cry shall fail.
“And the Egyptians will I give over into the hand of a cruel lord; and a fierce king shall rule over them.” That is this administration right now.
“He sent a man before them, even Joseph, who was sold for a servant: Whose feet they hurt with fetters: he was laid in iron.” Laid in iron means he was in chains.
“Until the time that his word came: the word of the Lord tried him. The king sent and loosed him”, and “made him lord of his house, and ruler of all his substance.”
“To bind his princes at his pleasure; and teach his senators wisdom.” Joseph taught the men of Egypt wisdom.

Jacob, now in Egypt, called his sons: “that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the last days.” Highlight those last words, in the last days. Christians read it and say it happened differently. It says in the last days. What don’t you understand about that?

“Joseph is a fruitful bough, even a fruitful bough by a well.” In the last days they would live by the water, on islands. “Whose branches run over the wall”: walls were built, like El Morro, the fort the white man built to keep other European countries from taking places like Puerto Rico. The branches running over the wall are the Puerto Rican people wanting to join with the European nations other than Spain.
“The archers have sorely grieved him, and shot at him, and hated him.” The conquistadors have sorely grieved him.
“But his bow abode in strength, and the arms of his hands were made strong by the hands of the mighty God of Jacob.”

“Blessings of heaven above” means good seasons, good climate, good weather. “Blessings of the deep that lieth under”: fish and gold and things beneath the waters. “Blessings of the breasts, and of the womb”: children upon children upon children.

“The blessings of thy father have prevailed above the blessings of my progenitors.” This is Jacob speaking: the blessings of Joseph prevailed above the blessings of Abraham and Isaac. None of what God promised Abraham, Isaac and Jacob was fulfilled at that time; Canaan was not ours yet. But Joseph ruled all Egypt. “They shall be on the head of Joseph, and on the crown of the head of him that was separate from his brethren.”

The Spanish records of the explorers bear it out. The Aztecs kept customs of a Judaic character. In Peru a Dominican friar, an Edomite, declared himself the Messiah and wanted a war to the death against the Indians because they were the lost tribes, to force Christ to come back. Indian guides spoke of a hidden people who would avenge them. And Indians recited the Shema Yisrael in Hebrew to the Marrano Montesinos and told him that they were of the tribe of Reuben and that the tribe of Joseph lived on an island nearby. That was Puerto Rico, with Manasseh in Cuba.

“They have taken crafty counsel against thy people, and consulted against thy hidden ones.” The Spanish records tell of an Indian guide who said his countrymen would be avenged upon the Spaniards in time by means of a people now hidden. That people now hidden is Judah. It is the same thing the book is saying: thy hidden ones.

The Spanish records say the sorcerers of the tribe warned that the God of these children of Israel is the true God, and that at the end of days they will be lords of all the nations of the earth and reign over the whole earth as they once did. That is what they don’t want.

“And the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High.” That is the whole earth. “Whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him.”
Moses blesses the twelve tribes before he dies.
“Blessed of the Lord be his land, for the precious things of heaven”: good weather, good climate. “For the deep that coucheth beneath”: the things in the ocean, the fish.

“The precious fruits brought forth by the sun, and for the precious things put forth by the moon.” There are things in Puerto Rico and Cuba that only come out by the moon, like the coquí frog, and things grown there that come out only by the full moon.

“The good will of him that dwelt in the bush.” That was Christ: the spirit of Christ was in the bush. “Let the blessing come upon the head of Joseph, and upon the top of the head of him that was separated from his brethren.”

“His glory is like the firstling of his bullock”: that is Ephraim. “His horns are like the horns of unicorns”: unicorn means rhinoceros. “With them he shall push the people together to the ends of the earth.” That is very important. Ephraim and Manasseh were used instrumentally by God to push the ten tribes from the eastern hemisphere to the western hemisphere. “They are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh.”

precepts.why:
“Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land”, and “he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.” They took counsel to “go forth into a further country, where never mankind dwelt, That they might there keep their statutes, which they never kept in their own land.”

“They entered into Euphrates by the narrow places of the river. For the most High then shewed signs for them, and held still the flood, till they were passed over.” It took a year and a half to travel, “and the same region is called Arsareth.” Arsareth is the region now called America.

That explains how Joseph’s horns pushed the people together to the ends of the earth: the ten tribes were pushed to the western hemisphere.

“They shall walk after the Lord: he shall roar like a lion: when he shall roar, then the children shall tremble from the west.” How did they get to the west? We just read it in Deuteronomy 33:17 and 2 Esdras 13. That is how they got to the western hemisphere over here.

sense.text: “Ephraim, he hath mixed himself among the people.” They like to say that is not talking about interracial mixing. Yes, it is. “Ephraim is a cake not turned”: some are very light, because they mixed with Esau, extremely light, some can pass for Esau; and some did not mix and are very dark.

“Strangers have devoured his strength, and he knoweth it not.” The white man has devoured Ephraim’s strength, and Ephraim does not realize it. “Gray hairs are here and there upon him, yet he knoweth not”: they grow old and don’t know their own history.

precepts.why: “For both they and their sons have married with their daughters, and the holy seed is mixed with the strange people of the land.” The holy seed is mixed. Ephraim mixing himself among the people is the holy seed marrying with the strange people of the land: interracial mixing.

sense.text: “They shall not dwell in the Lord’s land; but Ephraim shall return to Egypt.” That is what we read in Revelation 11:8: that great city which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt. “And they shall eat unclean things in Assyria.”

precepts.why: “Even thus shall the children of Israel eat their defiled bread among the Gentiles, whither I will drive them.” Just as Ephraim would eat unclean things in Assyria, so would all the tribes, among the Gentiles where they were driven.

sense.text: “As for Ephraim, their glory shall fly away like a bird, from the birth, and from the womb, and from the conception.”

“Ephraim, as I saw Tyrus, is planted in a pleasant place”: the pleasant place Moses and Jacob spoke of, the islands. “But Ephraim shall bring forth his children to the murderer.” Ephraim would willingly take their children to improve la raza: we want our race improved, we want our children to have straight hair, not that nappy hair, light skin and lighter eyes. That is what the Bible says Ephraim would do.

“Give them, O Lord: what wilt thou give? give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts.” God is saying a lot of those Edomite children, he will kill. So don’t worry, brothers, about whether you are talking to an Edomite. Just teach.

“Ephraim is smitten, their root is dried up, they shall bear no fruit: yea, though they bring forth, yet will I slay even the beloved fruit of their womb.” The ones that are out, that is Ephraim. You say, I think that is Esau. That is Ephraim.

“There was a certain man in Cesarea called Cornelius.” Look at the map of the Holy Land: Caesarea is right above Samaria on the coast. That is Manasseh’s land. That is where Cornelius was from. More proof that Cornelius was northern kingdom. Jump up and call him a goy all you want; do some research, do some study.
“A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway.”
When God accepted Cornelius and his kinsmen in Acts 10, then came Acts 15: “And to this agree the words of the prophets”: the prophets, in Amos.

“I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down.” That means bringing back the twelve tribes of Israel: the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom. Christians don’t realize what happened to the northern kingdom.

“That the residue of men might seek after the Lord”: they are going to seek him in slavery. “And all the Gentiles, upon whom my name is called”: those that call themselves Jewish and those that call themselves Christian.

precepts.why: “The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles.” The northern kingdom is what they called the Gentiles. Christians have not figured that out yet.

“In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof.” This is what James and Peter were quoting: he is going to bring back the southern kingdom with the northern kingdom, “and I will build it as in the days of old”.

“That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name.” Those are the ones who call themselves Jewish and call themselves Christian. Christian is a Greek word that means anointed ones. You are not the anointed ones. We are.

sense.text: “There were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.”
“Of the tribe of Manasses were sealed twelve thousand.” Manasseh is mentioned here.
“Of the tribe of Joseph were sealed twelve thousand.” Joseph is mentioned and Ephraim is not. Joseph here is Ephraim.

precepts.why: “Behold, I will take the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim.” The stick of Joseph is in the hand of Ephraim. That is how we know the tribe of Joseph sealed in Revelation 7 is Ephraim. “And the tribes of Israel his fellows, and will put them with him, even with the stick of Judah, and make them one stick, and they shall be one in mine hand.”

sense.text: Jacob has died, and now the brothers are scared Joseph is going to seek revenge: “Joseph will peradventure hate us, and will certainly requite us all the evil which we did unto him.”
“Fear not: for am I in the place of God?”

“But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.” This is the point. Only a spiritual man can understand that. Joseph was on another level when it came to understanding. He could sit back and reflect on all that happened to him and know it was God’s divine plan. He may not have understood it while he was in the midst of it, but going through seven years of plenty and seven years of famine he realized his purpose: God set the whole thing up.

precepts.why:
“And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.” We all go through things and might not understand them while we are going through: why is God doing this to me, why am I going through this and nobody else? There is a purpose.

All things means all things: poverty, health problems, eviction, trials, tribulations, temptations. Whatever it is, you have to endure it until the last end, and God is going to restore.

“And the Lord turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the Lord gave Job twice as much as he had before.” His brethren and sisters came, ate bread with him and comforted him “over all the evil that the Lord had brought upon him.”

“So the Lord blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning.” Endure to the end and God restores everything: the sheep, the camels, the oxen, seven sons and three daughters, and “in all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job.” As with Joseph, what was meant for evil God turned to good at the latter end.

“Ye that fear the Lord, wait for his mercy; and go not aside, lest ye fall.” Don’t go aside, wanting to leave this truth and do something else; you are going to fall. “Ye that fear the Lord, believe him; and your reward shall not fail.”

“Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in the Lord, and was confounded?” Was Job confounded? No. Was Joseph? “For the Lord is full of compassion and mercy, longsuffering, and very pitiful, and forgiveth sins, and saveth in time of affliction.”

sense.text: Back to Egypt. “I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee.” Seba is Somalia. Egypt, Ethiopia and Seba for us: that is the Nile.

“Since thou wast precious in my sight, thou hast been honourable, and I have loved thee.” The Israelites are precious in his sight. “Therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.” Give men for thee means kill men for thee. We don’t have to do nothing; God says, let me do it.

“I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west; I will say to the north, Give up; and to the south, Keep not back: bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth.”

precepts.why: “So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.” There can be no salvation without the destruction of your enemies, no salvation of the oppressed without the destruction of the oppressor. That is what it means that God will give men for thee and people for thy life. It is so plain, but for Christians it is so difficult to understand.

sense.text: “The envy also of Ephraim shall depart”: whatever the northern kingdom has against the southern kingdom must depart. “And the adversaries of Judah shall be cut off”: the enemies of Judah shall be cut off. “Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim.”

precepts.why: “Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart.” “Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am the Lord.” This is why Ephraim shall not envy Judah and Judah shall not vex Ephraim: the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom must apply this law if they want salvation.

“Master, which is the great commandment in the law?” First, “Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.” “And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.”

Your neighbour, as Leviticus 19 says, is the children of your people: your race. It is literally saying, love your race. No one is getting into the kingdom, no one is entering New Jerusalem, no one is making it out of the wilderness with hatred in his heart. Our people have not learned that. Look at South Africa: they love the white man more than their own brothers and sisters that look just like them. God’s laws must continue to be pushed and taught in this earth.

sense.text: “By the blood of thy covenant”: that is the new covenant, the blood of Christ. “I have sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit”: we are the prisoners. The pit is the same as the valley in Ezekiel 37; that pit is Babylon the Great. “Wherein is no water”: there is no truth in this land.

“Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope.” The strong hold is the Holy Bible. We are the prisoners of hope, hoping for New Jerusalem. Some of our people are hoping for equality. We are not hoping for no damn equality. We are hoping for supremacy. “I will render double unto thee.”

“When I have bent Judah for me”: he is going to bend Judah to his will. “Filled the bow with Ephraim, and raised up thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Greece”: he is going to raise up all twelve tribes against Esau. “And made thee as the sword of a mighty man”: he is going to transform us from these weak, frail bodies into the sword of a mighty man.

“And the Lord shall be seen over them.” This is how you know it is God’s doing: you are going to see the chariots of God above our heads. “His arrow shall go forth as the lightning”: lightnings coming forth in destruction. The whirlwinds of the south are the chariots.
“The Lord of hosts shall defend them”: the Lord of hosts shall defend us.

“The Lord their God shall save them in that day as the flock of his people”: we are the flock of his people. “For they shall be as the stones of a crown”: not brick, not cement, but rubies and jewels. That is how we are going to be, “lifted up as an ensign upon his land.”

precepts.why: “Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant.” That explains “by the blood of thy covenant” in Zechariah 9:11: it is the blood of Christ, the new covenant, by which the prisoners are sent forth out of the pit.

“For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.” We are holy, we are special unto God, above all people. Does it say equal? It says above.

That is why the prisoners of hope are not hoping for equality. The hell with your equality. Think about the white man’s words: when he says we are all equal, it translates to him on top and us on the bottom. It is all trickery when he speaks.
